title_guess: Food price indices WFPI and CFPI: why food-only indices exist beside WPI and CPI, what goes into their baskets, CFPI weights and how they are watched
recurring_cast: cart (wooden handcart piled with goods_boxes) labelled WPI
pink WFPI and CFPI cards on the two sides, ? marks later swapped for tick_marks
basket (wicker) sitting on each food-index card
pale yellow band around the two parent indices vs pink panels around the two food indices
wavy vertical separators between parents and children
learner_character (cartoon girl with a ? bubble) asking the why-question
white chip cards listing the commodity groups of WPI and CPI
running_examples: WPI's three groups: primary articles, manufactured products, fuel and power; only the first two hold food, so WFPI takes food articles from those two
CPI's six groups: only food and beverages is kept for CFPI; pan-tobacco, clothing-footwear, housing, fuel-light and miscellaneous are struck
CFPI weights table (10 subgroups x rural/urban/combined): cereals highest (26.14 rural), milk next (highest in urban, 17.98), vegetables (highest in rural, 15.78); each column sums to 100

best_moments.why: a wicker basket sits on each food index and a purple elbow arrow rises from the parent's 'food articles' tag and drops into it: a sub-index is a basket filled from the parent's food items
colour zones carry 'broad vs narrow': a pale yellow band wraps the WPI cart and CPI trolley (wide range of goods), pink panels wrap WFPI and CFPI (food only)
an India map stands on a pile of person icons ('food is most households' biggest expense'); an arrow from 'food index' lands on a green 'economic wellbeing' band and the crowd turns green
CPI's non-food groups are struck through one by one until only food and beverages is left, and that chip moves under CFPI: selection by elimination
both indices send green arrows up to a person at a wall of chart screens ('monitored'), and chevrons run on to the FCI emblem: data leads to an agency acting

weak_moments.why: about 25 s where the calculation formulas (named in speech as Laspeyres and Paasche) and food-price volatility are only spoken over a static holdover canvas; whether Paasche is used for these indices is doubtful and needs checking
a 10-row by 3-column weights table (30 numbers) for about 48 s; only 26.14 is read aloud, 17.98 and 15.78 are boxed but never spoken
the WPI and CPI group names are text chips; 'weighted arithmetic mean' is only written under the list, never shown working
the claim that big swings are passed to FCI so cheap grain reaches the vulnerable is shown only as an FCI logo; no grain, no people; the causal link is simplified and should be checked
app-promo phone slides over the canvas while the teaching is still on; channel banners sit at top and bottom of every frame

segments.teaches: WFPI and CFPI are the food-only partners of WPI and CPI; WPI and CPI already include food articles, which raises the question why separate food indices are needed

underline under the word Food in both full forms
big ? over WFPI and over CFPI

segments.notes: 5 change events (9.6, 11.4, 17.4, 23.8, 26.0). Wavy vertical lines separate the parents from the food indices. The ? marks pop exactly on the spoken word 'question'.
segments.idea: two new food indices sit beside the two familiar price indices, which already contain food, so why make food-only ones?

segments.teaches: WPI and CPI cover a wide range of goods and services; the food indices are limited to food items; the bigger question is why a separate food index matters

segments.teaches: WPI's three groups (primary articles, manufactured products, fuel and power) and CPI's six groups are recalled; food is found only in primary articles and manufactured products, so WFPI keeps those food articles with WPI's weights and a weighted arithmetic mean

segments.example: WPI groups: primary articles and manufactured products hold food; fuel and power does not

segments.example: of CPI's six groups only food and beverages survives
